strict_semver.description: If `true`, only stable semantic version tags are returned. Prerelease tags such as `1.2.3-rc.1` are excluded as well as any other tags that do not conform to the semantic versioning specification. Defaults to `false`.

tags.description: List of available Docker image tags matching the specified criteria.

disable_docker_daemon_check.description: If set to `true`, the provider will not check if the Docker daemon is running. This is useful for resources/data_sourcess that do not require a running Docker daemon, such as the data source `docker_registry_image`.

key_material.description: PEM-encoded content of Docker client private key

ssh_opts.description: Additional SSH option flags to be appended when using `ssh://` protocol

auth_disabled.description: Setting this to `true` will tell the provider that this registry does not need authentication. config_file.description: Path to docker json file for registry auth. Defaults to `~/.docker/config.json`. config_file_content.description: Plain content of the docker json file for registry auth. `config_file_content` has precedence over username/password.

username.description: Username for the registry. Defaults to `DOCKER_REGISTRY_USER` env variable if set.

bootstrap.description: Automatically boot the builder after creation. Defaults to `false`

use.description: Set the current builder instance as the default for the current context.

config_paths.description: One or more Compose file paths, equivalent to repeating the `-f` flag with `docker compose`.

env_files.description: Optional list of env files to load before parsing the Compose configuration. If omitted, Compose uses the default `.env` behavior.

id.description: The Compose project name used as the Terraform resource ID.

profiles.description: Optional list of Compose profiles to enable.

project_directory.description: Optional project directory used as the Compose working directory. If omitted, Compose uses the directory of the first file in `config_paths`.

project_name.description: Optional Compose project name. If omitted, Compose derives the project name the same way as the CLI.

remove_orphans.description: If `true`, remove containers for services that are no longer present in the Compose configuration during apply and destroy.

wait.description: If `true`, wait until services reach the running or healthy state before returning from apply.

wait_timeout.description: Optional duration for `wait`, for example `30s` or `2m`.

Manages the configs of a Docker service in a swarm.

attach.description: If `true` attach to the container after its creation and waits the end of its execution. Defaults to `false`.

bridge.description: The network bridge of the container as read from its NetworkSettings.

cgroup_parent.description: Optional parent cgroup for the container

cgroupns_mode.description: Cgroup namespace mode to use for the container. Possible values are: `private`, `host`.

command.description: The command to use to start the container. For example, to run `/usr/bin/myprogram -f baz.conf` set the command to be `["/usr/bin/myprogram","-f","baz.conf"]`.

container_logs.description: The logs of the container if its execution is done (`attach` must be disabled).

container_read_refresh_timeout_milliseco.description: The total number of milliseconds to wait for the container to reach status 'running'

cpu_period.description: Specify the CPU CFS scheduler period (in microseconds), which is used alongside `cpu-quota`. Is ignored if `cpus` is set.

cpu_quota.description: Impose a CPU CFS quota on the container (in microseconds). The number of microseconds per `cpu-period` that the container is limited to before throttled. Is ignored if `cpus` is set.

cpu_set.description: A comma-separated list or hyphen-separated range of CPUs a container can use, e.g. `0-1`.

cpu_shares.description: CPU shares (relative weight) for the container.

cpus.description: Specify how much of the available CPU resources a container can use. e.g a value of 1.5 means the container is guaranteed at most one and a half of the CPUs. Has precedence over `cpu_period` and `cpu_quota`.

destroy_grace_seconds.description: If defined will attempt to stop the container before destroying. Container will be destroyed after `n` seconds or on successful stop.

device_cgroup_rules.description: Cgroup rules to allow access to classes of devices without binding specific device nodes.

dns_opts.description: DNS options used by the DNS provider(s), see `resolv.conf` documentation for valid list of options.

dns_search.description: DNS search domains that are used when bare unqualified hostnames are used inside of the container.

entrypoint.description: The command to use as the Entrypoint for the container. The Entrypoint allows you to configure a container to run as an executable. For example, to run `/usr/bin/myprogram` when starting a container, set the entrypoint to be `"/usr/bin/myprogram"]`.

env.description: Environment variables to set in the form of `KEY=VALUE`, e.g. `DEBUG=0`

exit_code.description: The exit code of the container if its execution is done (`must_run` must be disabled).

gpus.description: GPU devices to add to the container. Supported values are `all` or `device=<id[,id...]>`, for example `device=0,2` or `device=GPU-3a23c669-1f69-c64e-cf85-44e9b07e7a2a`.

group_add.description: Additional groups for the container user

image.description: The ID of the image to back this container. The easiest way to get this value is to use the `image_id` attribute of the `docker_image` resource as is shown in the example.

init.description: Configured whether an init process should be injected for this container. If unset this will default to the `dockerd` defaults.

ipc_mode.description: IPC sharing mode for the container. Possible values are: `none`, `private`, `shareable`, `container:<name|id>` or `host`.

log_driver.description: The logging driver to use for the container.

log_opts.description: Key/value pairs to use as options for the logging driver.

logs.description: Save the container logs (`attach` must be enabled). Defaults to `false`.

max_retry_count.description: The maximum amount of times to an attempt a restart when `restart` is set to 'on-failure'.

memory.description: The memory limit for the container in MBs.

memory_reservation.description: The memory-resveration for the container in MBs. Defaults to 0. Allows you to specify a soft limit smaller than `memory` which is activated when Docker detects contention or low memory on the host machine. If you use `memory-reservation`, it must be set lower than `memory` for it to take precedence. Because it is a soft limit, it doesn't guarantee that the container doesn't exceed the limit.

memory_swap.description: The total memory limit (memory + swap) for the container in MBs. This setting may compute to `-1` after `terraform apply` if the target host doesn't support memory swap, when that is the case docker will use a soft limitation.

must_run.description: If `true`, then the Docker container will be kept running. If `false`, Terraform leaves the container alone. This attribute is also used to trigger a restart of a stopped container. If your container is stopped, Terraform will set `must_run` to `false` and this will trigger a change. Defaults to `true`.

name.description: The name of the container.

network_data.description: The data of the networks the container is connected to.

network_mode.description: Network mode of the container. Defaults to `bridge`. If your host OS is any other OS, you need to set this value explicitly, e.g. `nat` when your container will be running on an Windows host. See https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/ for more information.

pid_mode.description: The PID (Process) Namespace mode for the container. Either `container:<name|id>` or `host`.

platform.description: Platform in the format `os[/arch[/variant]]` used for image lookup and container runtime, for example `linux/amd64`.

privileged.description: If `true`, the container runs in privileged mode.

publish_all_ports.description: Publish all ports of the container.

read_only.description: If `true`, the container will be started as readonly. Defaults to `false`.

remove_volumes.description: If `true`, it will remove anonymous volumes associated with the container. Defaults to `true`.

restart.description: The restart policy for the container. Must be one of 'no', 'on-failure', 'always', 'unless-stopped'. Defaults to `no`.

rm.description: If `true`, then the container will be automatically removed when it exits. Defaults to `false`.

runtime.description: Runtime to use for the container.

security_opts.description: List of string values to customize labels for MLS systems, such as SELinux. See https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/run/#security-configuration.

start.description: If `true`, then the Docker container will be started after creation. If `false`, then the container is only created. Defaults to `true`.

stdin_open.description: If `true`, keep STDIN open even if not attached (`docker run -i`). Defaults to `false`.

stop_timeout.description: Timeout (in seconds) to stop a container.

storage_opts.description: Key/value pairs for the storage driver options, e.g. `size`: `120G`

sysctls.description: A map of kernel parameters (sysctls) to set in the container.

tmpfs.description: A map of container directories which should be replaced by `tmpfs mounts`, and their corresponding mount options.

tty.description: If `true`, allocate a pseudo-tty (`docker run -t`). Defaults to `false`.

user.description: User used for run the first process. Format is `user` or `user:group` which user and group can be passed literally or by name.

userns_mode.description: Sets the usernamespace mode for the container when usernamespace remapping option is enabled.

wait.description: If `true`, then the Docker container is waited for being healthy state after creation. This requires your container to have a healthcheck, otherwise this provider will error. If `false`, then the container health state is not checked. Defaults to `false`.

wait_timeout.description: The timeout in seconds to wait the container to be healthy after creation. Defaults to `60`.

working_dir.description: The working directory for commands to run in.

add.description: List of linux capabilities to add.

drop.description: List of linux capabilities to drop.

block.description: Add or drop certain linux capabilities.

path.description: The device path on the host, e.g. `/dev/sda`.

rate.description: The read rate limit in bytes per second.

block.description: Limit read rate (bytes per second) from a device. This is the equivalent to repeating `--device-read-bps` for `docker run`.

path.description: The device path on the host, e.g. `/dev/sda`.

block.description: Limit read rate (IO per second) from a device. This is the equivalent to repeating `--device-read-iops` for `docker run`.

capabilities.description: List of device capabilities. Only used with `nvidia` driver (e.g., `gpu`, `compute`, `utility`).

count.description: Number of devices to request. Use -1 for all devices. Only used with `nvidia` driver.

device_ids.description: List of device IDs or CDI device identifiers (e.g., `nvidia.com/gpu=all`).

driver.description: The device driver to use. Common values: `cdi` for CDI devices, `nvidia` for NVIDIA GPU requests.

block.description: Device requests for the container, such as CDI devices (e.g., `nvidia.com/gpu=all`) or GPU requests. This is the equivalent to using the `--device` flag for CDI devices in `docker run`.

path.description: The device path on the host, e.g. `/dev/sda`.

rate.description: The write rate limit in bytes per second.

block.description: Limit write rate (bytes per second) to a device. This is the equivalent to repeating `--device-write-bps` for `docker run`.

path.description: The device path on the host, e.g. `/dev/sda`.

block.description: Limit write rate (IO per second) to a device. This is the equivalent to repeating `--device-write-iops` for `docker run`.

container_path.description: The path in the container where the device will be bound. If not set, it defaults to the value of `host_path`.

host_path.description: The path on the host where the device is located.

permissions.description: The cgroup permissions given to the container to access the device. Defaults to `rwm`.

block.description: Bind traditional devices to the container (e.g., `/dev/nvidia0`). For CDI devices, use `device_requests` instead.

interval.description: Time between running the check (ms|s|m|h). Defaults to `0s`.

retries.description: Consecutive failures needed to report unhealthy. Defaults to `0`.

start_interval.description: Interval before the healthcheck starts (ms|s|m|h). Defaults to `0s`.

start_period.description: Start period for the container to initialize before counting retries towards unstable (ms|s|m|h). Defaults to `0s`.

test.description: Command to run to check health. For example, to run `curl -f localhost/health` set the command to be `["CMD", "curl", "-f", "localhost/health"]`. It works in the same way, and has the same default values, as the HEALTHCHECK Dockerfile instruction set by the service's Docker image. Your Compose file can override the values set in the Dockerfile.

timeout.description: Maximum time to allow one check to run (ms|s|m|h). Defaults to `0s`.

block.description: A test to perform to check that the container is healthy

ip.description: IP address this hostname should resolve to.

block.description: Additional hosts to add to the container.

source.description: Mount source (e.g. a volume name, a host path).

propagation.description: A propagation mode with the value.

block.description: Optional configuration for the bind type.

mode.description: The permission mode for the tmpfs mount in an integer.

size_bytes.description: The size for the tmpfs mount in bytes.

block.description: Optional configuration for the tmpfs type.

driver_name.description: Name of the driver to use to create the volume.

driver_options.description: key/value map of driver specific options.

no_copy.description: Populate volume with data from the target.

subpath.description: Path within the volume to mount. Requires docker server version 1.45 or higher.

Specification for mounts to be added to containers created as part of the service.

aliases.description: The network aliases of the container in the specific network.

driver_opts.description: An array of driver options for the network endpoint, e.g. `opts1=value`. This is the equivalent to repeating `--driver-opt` for `docker run`.

gw_priority.description: Gateway priority for this endpoint. The endpoint with the highest priority will provide the default gateway for the container. This is the equivalent to `--gw-priority` for `docker run`.

ipv4_address.description: The IPV4 address of the container in the specific network.

ipv6_address.description: The IPV6 address of the container in the specific network.

link_local_ips.description: The link-local IPs of the container in the specific network. This is the equivalent to repeating `--link-local-ip` for `docker run`.

mac_address.description: The MAC address of the container in the specific network.

name.description: The name or id of the network to use. You can use `name` or `id` attribute from a `docker_network` resource.

block.description: The networks the container is attached to. This is the equivalent to the ``--network`` option of `docker run`

external.description: Port exposed out of the container. If not given a free random port `>= 32768` will be used.

ip.description: IP address/mask that can access this port. Defaults to `0.0.0.0`.

protocol.description: Protocol that can be used over this port. Defaults to `tcp`.

block.description: Publish a container's port(s) to the host.

name.description: The name of the ulimit

block.description: Ulimit options to add.

content.description: Literal string value to use as the object content, which will be uploaded as UTF-8-encoded text. Conflicts with `content_base64` & `source`

content_base64.description: Base64-encoded data that will be decoded and uploaded as raw bytes for the object content. This allows safely uploading non-UTF8 binary data, but is recommended only for larger binary content such as the result of the `base64encode` interpolation function. See [here](https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-docker/issues/48#issuecomment-374174588) for the reason. Conflicts with `content` & `source`

executable.description: If `true`, the file will be uploaded with user executable permission. Defaults to `false`.

file.description: Path to the file in the container where is upload goes to

group.description: The group of the file in the container. Names are resolved using the Terraform host's group database; numeric IDs can be used directly.

owner.description: The owner of the file in the container. Names are resolved using the Terraform host's user database; numeric IDs can be used directly.

permissions.description: The permission mode for the file in the container. Has precedence over `executable`.

source.description: A filename that references a file which will be uploaded as the object content. This allows for large file uploads that do not get stored in state. Conflicts with `content` & `content_base64`

source_hash.description: If using `source`, this will force an update if the file content has updated but the filename has not.

block.description: Specifies files to upload to the container before starting it. Only one of `content` or `content_base64` can be set and at least one of them has to be set.

container_path.description: The path in the container where the volume will be mounted.

from_container.description: The container where the volume is coming from.

host_path.description: The path on the host where the volume is coming from. If `host_path` is set, it takes precedence over `volume_name`.

read_only.description: If `true`, this volume will be readonly. Defaults to `false`.

selinux_relabel.description: SELinux relabel mode for bind mounts. Supported values are `z` and `Z`.

volume_name.description: The name of the docker volume which should be mounted. Ignored when `host_path` is set.

block.description: Spec for mounting volumes in the container.
Manages the lifecycle of a Docker container.

force_remove.description: If true, then the image is removed forcibly when the resource is destroyed.

id.description: Unique identifier for this resource. This is not the image ID, but the ID of the resource in the Terraform state. This is used to identify the resource in the Terraform state. To reference the correct image ID, use the `image_id` attribute.

image_id.description: The ID of the image (as seen when executing `docker inspect` on the image). Can be used to reference the image via its ID in other resources.

keep_locally.description: If true, then the Docker image won't be deleted on destroy operation. If this is false, it will delete the image from the docker local storage on destroy operation.

name.description: The name of the Docker image, including any tags or SHA256 repo digests.

platform.description: The platform to use when pulling the image. Defaults to the platform of the current machine.

pull_triggers.description: List of values which cause an image pull when changed. This is used to store the image digest from the registry when using the [docker_registry_image](../data-sources/registry_image.md).

repo_digest.description: The image sha256 digest in the form of `repo[:tag]@sha256:<hash>`. This may not be populated when building an image, because it is read from the local Docker client and so may be available only when the image was either pulled from the repo or pushed to the repo (perhaps using `docker_registry_image`) in a previous run.

triggers.description: A map of arbitrary strings that, when changed, will force the `docker_image` resource to be replaced. This can be used to rebuild an image when contents of source code folders change

additional_contexts.description: A list of additional build contexts. Only supported when using a buildx builder. Example: `["name=path", "src = https://example.org"}`. Please see https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/build/#build-context for more information.

build_args.description: Pairs for build-time variables in the form of `ENDPOINT : "https://example.com"`

build_id.description: BuildID is an optional identifier that can be passed together with the build request. The same identifier can be used to gracefully cancel the build with the cancel request.

build_log_file.description: Path to a file where the buildx log are written to. Only available when `builder` is set. If not set, no logs are available. The path is taken as is, so make sure to use a path that is available.

builder.description: The name of the buildx builder to use. If BUILDX_BUILDER environment variable is set, it will be used. If left empty, the provider tries to resolve to the default builder - which might not always work. If you are in Windows, the legacy builder is used.

cache_from.description: External cache sources (e.g., `user/app:cache`, `type=local,src=path/to/dir`). Only supported when using a buildx builder.

cache_to.description: Cache export destinations (e.g., `user/app:cache`, `type=local,dest=path/to/dir`). Only supported when using a buildx builder.

cgroup_parent.description: Optional parent cgroup for the container

context.description: Value to specify the build context. Currently, only a `PATH` context is supported. You can use the helper function '${path.cwd}/context-dir'. This always refers to the local working directory, even when building images on remote hosts. Please see https://docs.docker.com/build/building/context/ for more information about build contexts.

cpu_period.description: The length of a CPU period in microseconds

cpu_quota.description: Microseconds of CPU time that the container can get in a CPU period

cpu_set_cpus.description: CPUs in which to allow execution (e.g., `0-3`, `0`, `1`)

cpu_set_mems.description: MEMs in which to allow execution (`0-3`, `0`, `1`)

dockerfile.description: Name of the Dockerfile. Defaults to `Dockerfile`.

extra_hosts.description: A list of hostnames/IP mappings to add to the container’s /etc/hosts file. Specified in the form ["hostname:IP"]

isolation.description: Isolation represents the isolation technology of a container. The supported values are

memory_swap.description: Total memory (memory + swap), -1 to enable unlimited swap

This resource manages the lifecycle of a Docker service. By default, the creation, update and delete of services are detached.
 With the [Converge Config](#convergeconfig) the behavior of the `docker cli` is imitated to guarantee tha for example, all tasks of a service are running or successfully updated or to inform `terraform` that a service could no be updated and was successfully rolled back.
